I'd like to take a trip through California and see the beaches along the way. What are some good places to visit? Places to find easy work, relaxed vibes, good people, warm year round weather?

The 5 cities area between Santa Maria and San Luis Obispo is REALLY nice/cool/laid back.

Pismo Beach is nearby, and still allows vehicles on the beach - so get that Jeep out and put the top down!

Close to SLO - less than 30 minutes) if you want to hang out for Farmer's market on Thursday. It's just 30 minutes or so from Paso Robles wine area, and there is also a winery (Laetitia) on the road to Santa Maria. Great steak joint down the road in Nipomo called "Jocko's"- worth the drive, and isn't really that pricey. All the steaks cooked over white oak. Also one in Arroyo Grande that was next to my hotel I frequented called AJ Spurs.

Hey that's cool to see Santa Maria mentioned, I was born there and lived the first few months of my life before moving up north out of state. Do you live there? What's the area like, would I find able to find an empty room on craiglist for pretty cheap or is it insanely expensive living there?

I'm tired of the Pac NW dreary clouds and rain and want to go south towards a more mild warm climate, preferably by the beach. I'm thinking about just taking a road trip through California along the coastline and maybe just plopping down wherever attracts me the most. I figured if I'm gonna be living pay check to pay check I might as well be doing so somewhere nice.

No, I spent two years in that area for a work project, and absolutely loved it. BUYING a place is pricey. Renting a room was not super difficult. Since the 5 cities isn't San Fran or LA, rents will all be for less than $1000/month, most in the $600-800 range. For California, that is not bad. But, you have the pick of 3 beaches, you have a nice downtown area, and grabbing a job didn't seem too difficult. People there really kind of go with the flow, pretty chill for the most part.

If you go up into SLO, you are looking at a higher per month rent, and Santa Maria is sort of in -between, but it's a lot further from the beaches than the 5 cities.

The weather is nice most of the year, sit out by a fire at night, maybe a light jacket or thin hoodie, lots of sunshine, and the hills are brown and gold. And there is FOOD being grown everywhere, so eating fresh is cheap and easy. If you want to hit the bars, they aren't going to knock you for $9 cocktails or $7 Bud Lights. More of a $4 Bud Light and $6 cocktail, so you can go out and drop $25 at a bar and catch a buzz. People are relatively friendly and open. Conversation is easy to start. People are for the most part fit and healthy, but maybe not the most beautiful in the world (not LA or Manhattan, for example.) They are more down-to-earth types, without being super hippies or judgemental.

If I had a place where I would want to retire, that or Grand Junction, CO are the two places I have enjoyed the most.
